package_info.why_malicious: These packages contain obfuscated JavaScript code that downloads and executes infostealer malware (Skuld and Blank Grabber) from external sources, enabling theft of credentials, personal files, and other sensitive data. The packages impersonate legitimate Roblox developer modules to trick users into installing them.

execution_context.file_location: index.js (main entry point of the npm package)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code downloads a Windows executable from a remote URL and executes it on the victim's machine, resulting in the installation of infostealer malware.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code automatically downloads and runs an external executable without user consent, a classic malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate npm packages should not download and execute arbitrary binaries during import or installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Auto-updaters or installers for legitimate software may download and run binaries, but only with explicit user consent and from trusted sources.
key_indicators: Network request to suspicious external URL

execution_context.file_location: index.js (main entry point of the npm package)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code downloads a secondary executable (cmd.exe) from a remote URL and executes it, potentially as a dropper or to escalate privileges.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and running a file named cmd.exe from an untrusted source is highly indicative of malicious intent, often used to establish persistence or run further payloads.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: npm packages should not fetch and execute system-level binaries from the internet.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, developer tools may fetch command-line utilities, but only from official sources and with user awareness.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the downloaded malware scans the victim's system for sensitive data (Discord tokens, browser credentials, crypto wallets) and exfiltrates it to a Discord webhook or via Telegram.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Infostealer behavior is inherently malicious, especially when exfiltrating credentials and personal data to attacker-controlled endpoints.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should deploy infostealer malware or exfiltrate user data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; only security tools with explicit user consent may scan for such data, and never exfiltrate it.
key_indicators: Use of known infostealer malware families

attack_chain.action: User installs or imports the malicious npm package (e.g., node-dlls, rolimons-api).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes on victim's machine.

attack_chain.action: Obfuscated JavaScript downloads and executes external malware payloads (RobloxPlayerLauncher.exe, cmd.exe) from attacker-controlled URLs.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware is installed and run on the victim's system.

attack_chain.action: Malware payload (Skuld infostealer, Blank Grabber) scans for sensitive data (credentials, tokens, wallets) and exfiltrates it to Discord webhook or Telegram.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen data; victim is compromised.

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated JavaScript in npm packages that downloads and executes external binaries
Automatic execution of downloaded files during import or installation
Network connections to suspicious or non-standard domains (e.g., github.com/zvydev/code)
Exfiltration of data to Discord webhooks or Telegram
file_indicators: index.js or main entry file containing obfuscated code
Creation of files named malware.exe or cmd.exe in the working directory
Presence of downloaded executables from github.com/zvydev/code
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm packages for obfuscated JavaScript that performs network requests to download and execute binaries. Flag packages that create or run executables during import or installation. Detect outbound connections to known malicious URLs or Discord webhooks. Alert on the presence of files named malware.exe or cmd.exe created by npm package processes. Use static and dynamic analysis to identify code that attempts to exfiltrate credentials or personal data.
